title: 第4157章 巡逻警戒 潜在威胁初现第4156章 剑阵护体 意外防患未然
slug: 签到玄天我成了万界守护者
content_zh:
方浩的脚步刚在主控通道口停稳，青铜鼎还贴在耳边听那机械傀儡传回来的嗡鸣声，就听见外舱合金门“哐”地一震，像是谁拿铁锤砸了口钟。
他没回头，只把鼎往怀里收了收：“又来？这回是蹭网还是试炮？”
话音未落，一道黄白相间的影子从门外窜进来，四爪踩地稳如老树盘根，正是剑齿虎。它鼻翼急张，耳朵向后一伏，喉咙里滚出低吼，尾巴绷得笔直，像根通了电的钢鞭。
方浩瞥它一眼：“你这表情，比上次黑焱偷吃供品被当场抓获时还严肃。”
剑齿虎不搭理这废话，前爪抬起，在地面划出三道弧线，又用鼻尖轻点其中一处，呼出一口凝实气流——那气流竟在空中颤出细密波纹，如同水面上被石子惊起的涟漪，但频率紊乱，断断续续。
方浩眯眼看了两息，伸手把青铜鼎翻了个面，底朝上轻轻一磕，鼎内传出“叮”一声脆响，像是应和。
“有点意思。”他低声说，“上回那股冲击是‘咚！咚！咚！’三下齐整，跟敲木鱼似的。你现在这动静，倒像是有人练功走火入魔，一边打嗝一边抖腿。”
剑齿虎甩了甩头，又低吼一声，这次声音压得更低，尾音拖长，明显是在强调：这不是故障，也不是自然波动，而是人为探测的残余信号，而且……还在持续。
方浩站直了些，原本懒散的肩背顿时绷紧。他低头看着鼎身，刚才那一声“叮”之后，鼎底浮现出一圈极淡的金纹，转瞬即逝，像是被什么东西扫过表面又被迅速抹去。
“看来真有人在外头搞副业。”他喃喃，“调试法器不选荒星野域，偏要蹭我们这艘二手星舰的壳子当试验场，属实是懒到家了。”
他抬脚往主控厅走，步伐不再拖沓，鞋底与金属板接触发出“哒、哒、哒”的清脆声响，每一步都像是踩在算盘珠子上，精准利落。
剑齿虎紧跟其后，耳朵始终朝外，眼睛盯着走廊尽头的观测窗。窗外漆黑一片，星点稀疏，可它仍能察觉到空间褶皱中那一丝不易察觉的扭曲——就像平静湖面下有鱼游过，虽不见形，却留痕。
方浩站在主控台前，抬手拍了三下台面，声音不大，却穿透力十足：“全员注意，二级戒备启动。”
广播系统“滋”地响了一声，随即响起机械女声：“警戒等级提升至二级，所有非核心岗位人员归位待命，防御力场检测程序自动激活。”
几盏红灯亮起，又缓缓转为琥珀色，整个星舰像是从打盹中睁开了半只眼。
“派三队机械傀儡，沿着外壳巡检一圈，重点查左舷第三至第七段护板接缝处。”方浩一边说，一边把青铜鼎放在台面上，双手按住鼎耳，闭眼听了片刻，“刚才那波动源，大概率是从那边渗进来的。”
鼎内传来细微的“沙沙”声，像是风吹过麦田，又像是某种远距离传讯的杂音。他知道这是傀儡小队正在反馈初步扫描结果。
“调过去三刻钟的所有空间监测记录。”他睁开眼，手指在台面上虚点两下，“我看看是不是有人装作路过，实则天天打卡签到。”
剑齿虎蹲在一旁合金平台上，前爪搭在边缘，目光死死锁住观测窗外的一角虚空。那里看似平静，但它能闻到一丝极淡的焦糊味——不是金属熔化的那种，更像是灵气燃烧过度后残留的灰烬气息，微弱，却带着人工雕琢的痕迹。
方浩低头翻看数据流，眉头越皱越紧。屏幕上滚动的画面显示，过去一个时辰内，星舰周围共记录到七次微幅震荡，间隔不等，但能量波形高度相似，尤其是第三次和第六次，几乎一致。

“这不是误触。”他冷笑一声，“这是在做AB测试呢。第一次力度太轻，第二次加了点劲，第三次找到了手感，第四次开始记笔记……简直把我们当免费测距仪用了。”
他转身抓起青铜鼎，顺手在鼎身上拍了两下，像是给自家狗顺毛：“行吧，既然人家这么看得起咱们，那就别光站着挨打。通知下去，外壳力场调成‘蜂窝模式’，每隔三十息随机变换一次频率，谁再想蹭数据，就得自己解密码。”
说完，他又看了眼剑齿虎：“你继续盯外头，有新动静立刻示警。别怕吵，反正现在没人睡觉。”
剑齿虎低吼一声，算是回应，尾巴轻轻一甩，重新凝神望向窗外。
方浩站在主控台前，一只手搭在鼎上，另一只手插进袖子里，神情不再嬉笑，眼角微微下压，像是集市里突然收起秤杆的奸商，表面不动声色，心里已经开始盘账。
远处，机械傀儡的扫描光束正一寸寸滑过星舰外壳，像是一群不知疲倦的工蚁在检查巢穴边界。而那片漆黑的虚空中，某处空间褶皱轻微晃动了一下，仿佛有人轻轻合上了笔记本，然后悄然退场。
方浩忽然开口：“下次要是再震，别急着报我。”
剑齿虎耳朵一抖。
“直接放预警音，响得让全舰人都以为食堂开饭了。”他嘴角微扬，“就说——今日特供，香煎灵能波动，限量三百份，先到先得。”

content_en:
As soon as Fang Hao's footsteps came to a stop at the entrance of the main control passage, and the bronze tripod was still pressed against his ear to listen to the buzzing sound coming from the mechanical puppet, he heard the outer cabin's alloy door shake with a "clang", as if someone had hit a bell with a hammer.
He didn't look back, he just put the tripod into his arms: "Again? Is this the net or the cannon test?"
Before he finished speaking, a yellow and white shadow rushed in from outside the door. Its four claws were as firm as the roots of an old tree. It was a saber-toothed tiger. Its nostrils flared, its ears fell back, a low growl rolled out of its throat, and its tail was stretched straight, like an electric steel whip.
Fang Hao glanced at it: "Your expression is more serious than the last time Hei Yan was caught stealing an offering."
The saber-toothed tiger ignored this nonsense, raised his front paws, drew three arcs on the ground, tapped one of them with the tip of his nose, and exhaled a breath of solid air - the air actually trembled in the air with fine ripples, like ripples on the water surface caused by stones, but the frequency was disordered and intermittent.
Fang Hao squinted for a moment, then stretched out his hand to turn the bronze cauldron over, and gently knocked it upside down. A crisp "ding" sound came from the cauldron, as if in response.
"It's interesting." He whispered. "Last time, the impact was 'Boom! Boom! Boom!' three times in a row, like knocking on a wooden fish. What you are doing now seems like someone who went crazy while practicing, hiccupping and shaking his legs."
The saber-toothed tiger shook his head and roared again. This time the voice was lower and the tail sound was longer, obviously emphasizing that this was not a malfunction or a natural fluctuation, but a residual signal of human detection, and... it was still going on.
Fang Hao stood up straighter, and his originally lazy shoulders suddenly became tense. He looked down at the cauldron. After the "ding" just now, a very faint golden pattern appeared on the bottom of the cauldron. It disappeared in an instant, as if something had been swept across the surface and then quickly wiped away.
"It seems that someone is really doing a side job outside." He murmured, "Instead of choosing the wilderness to debug the magic weapon, I chose to use the shell of our second-hand starship as a testing ground. I am really lazy."
He lifted his feet and walked towards the main control room, his steps no longer dragging. The soles of his shoes made a crisp sound of "ta, da, da" when they came into contact with the metal plate. Every step was like stepping on abacus beads, precise and neat.
The saber-toothed tiger followed closely, his ears always pointed outward and his eyes fixed on the observation window at the end of the corridor. It was pitch black outside the window, and the stars were sparse, but it could still detect the subtle distortion in the folds of space - just like a fish swimming under the surface of a calm lake. Although it was invisible, it left traces.
Fang Hao stood in front of the main console, raised his hand and patted the table three times. His voice was not loud, but it was very penetrating: "Attention, everyone, the second level alert is activated."
The PA system buzzed, and then a mechanical female voice sounded: "The alert level has been raised to Level 2, all non-core personnel are on standby, and the defensive force field detection program is automatically activated."
Several red lights turned on, then slowly turned to amber, and the entire starship seemed to have half opened its eyes from a nap.
"Send three teams of mechanical puppets to inspect the outer shell, focusing on the joints of the third to seventh sections of the port side guard." Fang Hao said while placing the bronze tripod on the table, pressing the tripod's ears with both hands, closing his eyes and listening for a moment, "The source of the wave just now most likely seeped in from there."
A subtle "rustling" sound came from the cauldron, like the wind blowing through the wheat field, or like the noise of some kind of long-distance communication. He knew that this was the puppet team feeding back preliminary scan results.
"Calling up all the space monitoring records for the past three quarters of an hour." He opened his eyes and tapped his fingers twice on the table. "I'll see if anyone is pretending to be passing by, but actually checking in every day."
The saber-toothed tiger crouched on the alloy platform aside, with his front paws on the edge, and his eyes fixed on the void in the corner of the observation window. It seems peaceful there, but it can smell a very faint smell of burnt metal - not the kind of melted metal, but more like the smell of ashes left after excessive burning of spiritual energy, faint, but with an artificially carved smell.trace.
Fang Hao lowered his head and looked through the data stream, frowning more and more. The scrolling picture on the screen showed that in the past hour, a total of seven micro-amplitude oscillations were recorded around the starship, with varying intervals, but the energy waveforms were highly similar, especially the third and sixth times, which were almost identical.
"This is not an accidental touch." He sneered, "This is an AB test. The first time the force was too light, the second time I added a little more force, the third time I found the feel, and the fourth time I started taking notes... We were basically used as free rangefinders."
He turned around, grabbed the bronze cauldron, and patted the cauldron twice, as if grooming his own dog: "Okay, since people think so highly of us, don't just stand and get beaten. We will inform you that the shell force field will be adjusted to 'cellular mode', and the frequency will be randomly changed every thirty breaths. Anyone who wants to use the data will have to decrypt the code themselves."
After saying that, he glanced at the saber-toothed tiger again: "You continue to stare outside and alert you immediately if there is any new movement. Don't be afraid of noise, no one is sleeping now anyway."
The saber-toothed tiger roared in response, flicked its tail, and looked out the window again.
Fang Hao stood in front of the main console, with one hand on the tripod and the other hand in his sleeve. His expression was no longer playful, and the corners of his eyes were slightly lowered, like a profiteer who suddenly put away the scale beam in the market. He was calm on the surface, but he had already begun to make an inventory in his heart.
In the distance, the scanning beam of the mechanical puppet was sliding across the shell of the starship inch by inch, like a group of tireless worker ants checking the boundaries of the nest. And in that pitch-black void, somewhere the spatial folds swayed slightly, as if someone gently closed the notebook and then quietly exited.
Fang Hao suddenly said: "If it happens again next time, don't be in a hurry to retaliate against me."
The saber-toothed tiger's ears twitched.
"Just play the warning sound. It was so loud that everyone on the ship thought that the cafeteria was open for dinner." He raised the corner of his mouth slightly, "Just say - today's special offer, pan-fried pan-fried psionic wave, limited to 300 servings, first come, first served."
